breaking_news.headline: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
breaking_news.summary: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.

breaking_news.headline: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
breaking_news.summary: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman

breaking_news.headline: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
breaking_news.summary: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

breaking_news.headline: What expensive sulfur means for your dinner table
breaking_news.summary: Oil supplies are falling, sulfur prices are threatening food costs, and we measure Lego against Hollywood

breaking_news.headline: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
breaking_news.summary: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.

breaking_news.headline: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
breaking_news.summary: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

breaking_news.headline: How a pizza app changed our relationship with waiting
breaking_news.summary: Status trackers are ubiquitous on online apps and ordering. We have the story the seminal Domino's Pizza Tracker that led to many copies, and we check on why many of the trackers now aren't accurate.

breaking_news.headline: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
breaking_news.summary: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.

breaking_news.headline: Saudi Arabia issues first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthis escalated attacks
breaking_news.summary: Residents later received the all-clear after explosions were reported in the capital.

breaking_news.headline: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
breaking_news.summary: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.

breaking_news.headline: Deadly shark attack prompts rare kill order in Western Australia
breaking_news.summary: Police boats and helicopters are patrolling Perth's beaches as authorities continue their search for the swimmer's body, and the shark that attacked him.

breaking_news.headline: Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa
breaking_news.summary: Dineo Motapane is one of nine recent victims whose deaths have left a nation traumatised over the level of violence against women.

breaking_news.headline: Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions bill
breaking_news.summary: The bill is named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch advocate of aid for Ukraine.

breaking_news.headline: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
breaking_news.summary: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.

breaking_news.headline: Trump says he is banning CNN and Politico from White House
breaking_news.summary: The US president has had a tense and fiery relationship with the US media throughout his political career.

breaking_news.headline: US and Denmark reach deal over Greenland after Trump annexation threats
breaking_news.summary: Trump says the agreement will give the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland", though specifics have not been confirmed by Danish officials.

breaking_news.headline: Thames Water rescue deal should be rejected - MPs
breaking_news.summary: A report on the future of Thames Water, urging the government to take action, has been published.

breaking_news.headline: British Steel plan lacks credibility, MPs say
breaking_news.summary: A committee report says the government has not set out how British Steel will become profitable.

breaking_news.headline: The virtual worlds where robots are trained
breaking_news.summary: Training systems that allow robots to negotiate the real world are getting more sophisticated.

breaking_news.headline: We bought our £242,000 home without a deposit - here's how
breaking_news.summary: The share of UK mortgages with smaller deposits is the highest it's been since 2008. The BBC spoke to borrowers about how they manage the risks.
